summary: The 12-month Enrollment survey covers institutional activity from July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, using institution-level reporting for undergraduate and graduate enrollment and instructional activity. It applies to eligible postsecondary institutions reporting students served or instructional activity during the full 12-month period, including institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs. The survey supports both unduplicated enrollment counts and instructional-activity measures used to derive full-time-equivalent enrollment.

This Completions component covers certificates and degrees awarded by postsecondary institutions during July 1, 2015–June 30, 2016, for institutions eligible or required to report IPEDS completions data. The unit of observation is the institution, with some tables repeating institutions by program or award level; the component covers all reported awards in the survey universe, with no additional survey-wide population restriction stated.

Fall Enrollment reports students enrolled at participating IPEDS postsecondary institutions. Traditional-calendar institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The unit is the institution, with multiple records when enrollment is broken out by student characteristics or levels; eligibility and available measures vary by institution type and program offerings.

The Finance survey was collected from December 2016 through April 2017 and reports each institution’s most recent fiscal year ending between July 1, 2015, and June 30, 2016. Its universe is Title IV-participating postsecondary institutions operating during the reporting period, with finance data reported at the institution level under the accounting standards applicable to the institution. Fiscal year 2016 data no longer include detailed expenditures by function or the natural classifications of fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest.

Graduation Rates is collected annually in the IPEDS winter collection and reports cohort outcomes as of August 31 of the survey year. The unit of observation is an eligible postsecondary institution’s cohort or cohort-status record, covering full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at institutions with applicable undergraduate programs. Results describe completion and transfer outcomes for defined entering cohorts, not all enrolled students; the applicable institution sector and cohort vary by table.

Human Resources data cover staff on the institution’s payroll as of November 1 for fall collections, while salary tables cover the associated academic year. Records are institution-level and may contain multiple rows per institution, identified by UNITID plus a table-specific occupational, rank, tenure, or other category. Eligibility varies by table; some staff tables are limited to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, while the other tables do not state that restriction.

The Institutional Characteristics component was collected during the fall 2016 collection window for academic year 2016-17, with institutions reporting institution-level characteristics and charges under the applicable IPEDS reporting dates and calendar rules. Its universe is the 2016 IPEDS universe of postsecondary institutions; active institutions participating in Title IV federal aid programs are required to report, while other eligible institutions may be included under applicable participation rules. Records generally represent an institution or reporting entity, and a parent institution may report for multiple campuses.

These institution-level data cover aid and benefits received during July 1, 2015–June 30, 2016, reported by eligible postsecondary institutions for their undergraduate and, where applicable, graduate students. The Student Financial Aid component is generally reported annually; the military servicemember and veteran benefits collection is biennial and applies only to institutions in the IPEDS reporting universe that offer the relevant students or programs.
